concepts.title: Comparing Numbers
concepts.description: Comparing numbers using place value, ordering numbers from smallest to largest and vice versa.
key_ideas: Numbers with more digits are always greater
Compare leftmost digits first when digit count is same
Ascending and descending order

concepts.title: Large Numbers and Indian Place Value System
concepts.description: Reading and writing large numbers in Indian system (Lakhs, Crores) and International system (Millions, Billions).
key_ideas: Indian system: Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Ten Thousands, Lakhs, Ten Lakhs, Crores
International system: Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Ten Thousands, Hundred Thousands, Millions
Using commas to separate periods

concepts.title: Estimation and Rounding Off
concepts.description: Rounding numbers to the nearest tens, hundreds, thousands. Estimating sums, differences, and products.
key_ideas: Rounding rules: 5 or more rounds up, less than 5 rounds down
Estimating to check reasonableness of answers
Practical use in daily life calculations

concepts.title: Roman Numerals
concepts.description: Reading and writing Roman numerals (I to C). Rules of Roman numeral system.
key_ideas: Basic symbols: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100
Addition rule: VI=6, Subtraction rule: IV=4
No symbol repeats more than 3 times

concepts.title: Natural Numbers and Whole Numbers
concepts.description: Understanding the number line, natural numbers (1,2,3...) and whole numbers (0,1,2,3...). The predecessor and successor of a number.
key_ideas: Whole numbers include 0 plus all natural numbers
Every whole number has a successor
Every whole number except 0 has a predecessor
Number line representation

concepts.title: Properties of Whole Numbers
concepts.description: Closure, commutativity, associativity, distributivity, and identity properties for addition and multiplication.
key_ideas: Closure: whole numbers are closed under addition and multiplication
Commutativity: a+b=b+a, a×b=b×a
Associativity: (a+b)+c=a+(b+c)
Distributivity: a×(b+c)=a×b+a×c
Additive identity is 0, multiplicative identity is 1

concepts.title: Patterns in Whole Numbers
concepts.description: Number line patterns, dot patterns, and other arrangements. Connecting geometry and numbers.
key_ideas: Triangular numbers: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15...
Square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25...
Patterns help predict and generalize

concepts.title: Factors and Multiples
concepts.description: Finding all factors of a number, listing multiples, understanding the relationship between factors and multiples.
key_ideas: A factor divides a number exactly
Every number is a factor of itself; 1 is a factor of every number
Multiples are obtained by multiplying by 1, 2, 3...
Number of factors is finite; multiples are infinite

concepts.title: Prime and Composite Numbers
concepts.description: Prime numbers have exactly 2 factors. Composite numbers have more than 2. Sieve of Eratosthenes.
key_ideas: 2 is the smallest and only even prime number
1 is neither prime nor composite
Sieve of Eratosthenes to find primes
Every composite number can be written as product of primes

concepts.title: Divisibility Rules
concepts.description: Tests of divisibility for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11.
key_ideas: Divisible by 2: last digit is even
Divisible by 3: sum of digits divisible by 3
Divisible by 5: ends in 0 or 5
Divisible by 9: sum of digits divisible by 9
Divisible by 11: difference of alternating sums is 0 or divisible by 11

concepts.title: HCF and LCM
concepts.description: Finding HCF by prime factorization and listing factors. Finding LCM by prime factorization and common multiples. HCF × LCM = Product of two numbers.
key_ideas: HCF: highest common factor — largest number that divides both
LCM: least common multiple — smallest number divisible by both
Prime factorization method
HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b

concepts.title: Points, Lines, Line Segments, and Rays
concepts.description: Basic building blocks of geometry. A point has no dimension. A line extends infinitely. A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint.
key_ideas: A point determines a location
Infinite lines through a point, exactly one through two points
Line segment = part of line with two endpoints
Ray = starts at a point and goes on forever in one direction

concepts.title: Curves, Polygons, and Angles
concepts.description: Open and closed curves, simple and non-simple curves. Polygons (triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon etc.). Angles and their classification.
key_ideas: Simple curve: doesn't cross itself
Polygon: closed simple curve made of line segments
Angle: formed by two rays with common endpoint (vertex)
Interior and exterior of an angle

concepts.title: Triangles and Circles
concepts.description: Parts of a triangle (vertices, sides, angles, medians, altitudes). Parts of a circle (center, radius, diameter, chord, arc, sector, segment).
key_ideas: Triangle has 3 vertices, 3 sides, 3 angles
Median connects vertex to midpoint of opposite side
Circle: all points equidistant from center
Diameter = 2 × Radius, Chord, Arc, Sector

concepts.title: Measuring Line Segments and Angles
concepts.description: Using ruler to measure line segments. Using protractor to measure angles. Types of angles: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex.
key_ideas: Acute: < 90°, Right: = 90°, Obtuse: 90°-180°
Straight: = 180°, Reflex: 180°-360°
Using protractor correctly

concepts.title: Perpendicular and Parallel Lines
concepts.description: Perpendicular lines meet at 90°. Parallel lines never meet. Identifying them in everyday objects.
key_ideas: Perpendicular: two lines at right angles
Parallel: same direction, never intersect
Real-world examples: railway tracks (parallel), corner of a room (perpendicular)

concepts.title: Classification of Triangles
concepts.description: Classifying triangles by sides (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) and by angles (acute, right, obtuse).
key_ideas: By sides: Scalene (all different), Isosceles (two equal), Equilateral (all equal)
By angles: Acute (all < 90°), Right (one = 90°), Obtuse (one > 90°)
Equilateral triangle is always acute

concepts.title: Quadrilaterals and Polygons
concepts.description: Types of quadrilaterals (rectangle, square, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium). Regular polygons.
key_ideas: Rectangle: opposite sides equal, all angles 90°
Square: all sides equal, all angles 90°
Parallelogram: opposite sides parallel and equal
Rhombus: all sides equal (parallelogram), Trapezium: one pair of parallel sides

concepts.title: Three-Dimensional Shapes
concepts.description: Cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, prisms, pyramids. Faces, edges, vertices.
key_ideas: 3D shapes have faces, edges, and vertices
Cube: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices
Euler's formula: F + V - E = 2
Nets of 3D shapes

concepts.title: Introduction to Integers
concepts.description: Negative numbers in real life (temperature, altitude, debt). Number line extending to the left. Integers = {..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.
key_ideas: Negative numbers represent below zero, debt, below sea level
Number line: negatives to the left, positives to the right
0 is neither positive nor negative

concepts.title: Addition and Subtraction of Integers
concepts.description: Adding and subtracting positive and negative numbers using number line. Rules for addition and subtraction of integers.
key_ideas: Same sign: add magnitudes, keep the sign
Different signs: subtract magnitudes, take sign of larger magnitude
Subtracting an integer = adding its additive inverse
a - (-b) = a + b

concepts.title: Understanding Fractions
concepts.description: Fraction as part of a whole. Numerator and denominator. Representing fractions on number line.
key_ideas: Fraction = part/whole
Numerator (top): parts taken, Denominator (bottom): total equal parts
Proper fractions: numerator < denominator
Improper fractions and mixed numbers

concepts.title: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.description: Fractions that represent the same value. Simplest form. Finding equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number.
key_ideas: Multiply/divide both parts by same number
Simplest form: HCF of numerator and denominator is 1
Cross multiplication to check equivalence

concepts.title: Comparing and Ordering Fractions
concepts.description: Comparing like fractions, unlike fractions. Converting to like fractions using LCM. Ordering fractions.
key_ideas: Like fractions: same denominator — compare numerators
Unlike fractions: find LCM of denominators, convert, then compare
Ascending and descending order of fractions

concepts.title: Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
concepts.description: Adding and subtracting like and unlike fractions. Adding and subtracting mixed numbers.
key_ideas: Like fractions: add/subtract numerators, keep denominator
Unlike fractions: convert to like fractions first (LCM)
Mixed numbers: convert to improper, operate, convert back
Always simplify the result

concepts.title: Introduction to Decimals
concepts.description: Decimals as fractions with denominator 10, 100, 1000. Place value in decimals (tenths, hundredths, thousandths). Reading and writing decimals.
key_ideas: Tenths = 1/10 = 0.1, Hundredths = 1/100 = 0.01
Place value extends to the right of decimal point
Decimals on the number line
Converting fractions to decimals and vice versa

concepts.title: Comparing Decimals
concepts.description: Comparing decimal numbers. Arranging in ascending/descending order. Using decimals in money, length, weight.
key_ideas: Compare whole number part first, then tenths, hundredths...
Adding trailing zeros doesn't change value: 2.5 = 2.50
Real-world: ₹45.50, 3.5 km, 1.25 kg

concepts.title: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals
concepts.description: Adding and subtracting decimals by aligning decimal points. Word problems involving money, measurements.
key_ideas: Align decimal points vertically
Add trailing zeros to make same number of decimal places
Real-world problems with money and measurements

concepts.title: Data Collection and Organization
concepts.description: Collecting data, organizing into tables, tally marks, frequency tables.
key_ideas: Data: information collected for analysis
Tally marks for counting
Frequency table organizes data
Raw data vs organized data

concepts.title: Pictographs
concepts.description: Reading and drawing pictographs. Using symbols to represent data. Interpreting pictographs.
key_ideas: Each symbol represents a fixed number
Key/legend tells what each symbol represents
Half symbols for half values
Drawing pictographs from given data

concepts.title: Bar Graphs
concepts.description: Reading and drawing bar graphs. Choosing appropriate scale. Interpreting bar graphs to answer questions.
key_ideas: Bars represent quantities, height = value
Equal width bars, equal gaps
Choosing scale based on data range
Horizontal and vertical bar graphs

concepts.title: Perimeter
concepts.description: Perimeter as the total boundary length. Perimeter of rectangles, squares, triangles, and regular polygons.
key_ideas: Perimeter = sum of all sides
Rectangle: 2(l+b), Square: 4×side
Equilateral triangle: 3×side
Regular polygon: n × side

concepts.title: Area
concepts.description: Area as the measure of surface. Area of rectangles and squares using formulas. Area using grid/graph paper.
key_ideas: Area = amount of surface enclosed
Rectangle: l×b, Square: side×side
Counting squares on grid paper for irregular shapes
Units: sq cm, sq m, sq km

concepts.title: Introduction to Variables and Expressions
concepts.description: Using letters to represent unknown numbers. Variables vs constants. Writing simple algebraic expressions.
key_ideas: Variable: a letter that represents an unknown or changing quantity
Expression: combination of variables, constants, and operations
Examples: x+3, 2n, 5y-1
Translating word statements to expressions

concepts.title: Simple Equations
concepts.description: Equations as statements of equality with a variable. Solving simple equations by trial-and-error and systematic methods.
key_ideas: Equation: expression = value, with a variable
LHS = RHS when variable has the correct value
Solution: the value that satisfies the equation
Trial and error, then systematic approach

concepts.title: Ratio
concepts.description: Ratio as comparison of two quantities. Simplest form of ratio. Equivalent ratios.
key_ideas: Ratio compares two quantities of same kind
Written as a:b or a/b
Order matters: a:b ≠ b:a
Simplest form: divide by HCF

concepts.title: Proportion
concepts.description: Proportion as equality of two ratios. Unitary method. Solving word problems using proportion.
key_ideas: a:b :: c:d means a/b = c/d
Cross multiplication: a×d = b×c
Unitary method: find value of 1 unit first
Real-world: recipes, maps, scale drawings

concepts.title: Line Symmetry
concepts.description: Line of symmetry divides a figure into two identical halves. Finding lines of symmetry in shapes and letters.
key_ideas: Line of symmetry: fold line that makes two matching halves
Some shapes have multiple lines of symmetry
Circle has infinite lines of symmetry
Regular polygons: n lines of symmetry

concepts.title: Basic Constructions
concepts.description: Using ruler and compass to construct: a circle, a line segment of given length, copy of a line segment, perpendicular bisector, angle bisector, angles of 60°, 120°, 90°, 30°, 45°.
key_ideas: Tools: ruler, compass, protractor, set squares
Perpendicular bisector: equidistant from both endpoints
Angle bisector: divides angle into two equal parts
Constructing standard angles with compass only
